newsitem.title: USA: Reward offered for arrest of California bomber.
newsitem.headline: Reward offered for arrest of California bomber.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson Wednesday offered a $50,000 reward to help investigators find those responsible for a firebomb attack that injured an anti-drug activist.

Hospital officials said Stevie Allman, 52, was listed in good condition. She suffered first and second degree burns over 15 percent of her body in the July 1 firebombing of her Oakland, California, home.
Wilson, a Republican, said Allman was a model neighbourhood activist who worked with local police for the past year to combat drug-dealing in the area.

"I want to send a loud, clear message to criminals and thugs that today Stevie Allman's neighbours, her community, her mayor, her police chief, and her governor stand with her," Wilson said in a statement announcing the $50,000 reward.

"All of us are sending a message that we will not be prisoners in our own homes -- cowering under our windows and behind steel bars. We will stand up for our families, neighbours and communities," Wilson said.
The July 1 firebombing was the third attack in three years in which Allman's home was targeted by drug dealers in retaliation for her anti-crime efforts, according to the Oakland Tribune newspaper.

"It is difficult to imagine people could be this cruel -- not once, not twice, but three times," Allman said in a statement. Her home was almost completely destroyed and her two dogs were killed in the fire.
